title: Still watching?: CEO says you shouldn’t give up on Netflix yet
transcript_text: Three and a half minutes before the closing bell rings and mostly markets are in the red. We do have the Dow at a record, though, up 35 points. S&P down 10, NASDAQ down 151. Russell can't quite make it. It's down 9 points, transports up 213. Netflix stock has been anything but binge worthy lately. Shares of the streaming platform have lost around 45% over the past year. But our countdown closer says, don't cancel the stock subscription yet. It actually might be a buying opportunity. Joining me now, infrastructure capital management, CEO J Hatfield, four billion in assets under management. People were saying it was a buy at 87. It's not 78. Well we've been adding to it recently in QVAL, which is our NASDAQ income fund. And the reason for that is we think it's been kind of double hammered for no particular reason. So they're going to complete a merger that thankfully didn't go through. And then the more importantly, this true for really many, many stocks in the NASDAQ is hedge funds way over did this trade of buying chips and selling everything else. So these companies have tremendously attractive peg ratios. So PE to growth, really good growth. And so what that they don't sell chips and chips are very cyclical risky business. So this is a much more stable business with way lower PEs and about 30% upside in our models. Let's not gloss over your QVAL fund, QVOL is the ticker. This eliminates what you call the dogs of the DAC, dogs of the NASDAQ. Right. Some of the other names of the dogs that you feel don't need to be included in the sort of hot and up and coming names or the ones that can re-inflate Tesla, Comcast, Charter, Craftines, Mondalees, Walmart, Costco. Interestingly, Walmart is the second worst performer on the Dow right now. And the Dow is struggling to even hold on to anything in the red. It just turned negative slightly. It's still up about three points. But you eliminate those names. Yes. So for two reason one, when you buy the NASDAQ, you really don't want Walmart and Craftines. Like you're looking for growth stocks with great long-term growth prospects. But more importantly with Walmart, we mentioned it in the context of Amazon. Like, why do you want to pay four and a half times growth for Walmart and one times growth for PE to growth for Amazon? So it made no sense. And actually, we don't do long-term, we kind of do because we have none of it in the NASDAQ. But if you look, Amazon is significantly outperforming Walmart, even though Amazon's down because it's being dragged into this sell everything in favor of chips. Let me just quickly say we've got about 40 seconds left. You had made a call several weeks ago, I believe, saying, oil is going to drop like a rock. This was when it was pretty high. It's been a good trade for you. Were you shorting crude? We were, and we think we'll get to 60, and there's one and only one reason. OPEC is producing a max production. That's 33 million berries. The barrels are usually going to do 29. And Iran is able to sell their oil all throughout the world freely now. You got eight bucks to go because it's 68 even right now in the after market. J, it's good to see you. Thank you very much. Happy Fourth of July weekend. Thanks, let's enjoy. Good to have you. All right, folks. The Dow barely in the green up 11 points was barely, but just a second ago, it's gone negative. There's the closing bell up. There it goes. Not a record down four points in this last couple of seconds. All of the majors in the red, but we'll see you tomorrow for the big show.
